implementation_notes: The delegate is an ordinary interface implemented by a hand-written class that receives a configured HttpClient by constructor injection; AddHttpClient<IBillingApi, BillingApi> registers the pair and lets IHttpClientFactory own handler pooling, base address, default headers and resilience policies. What replaces the classic structure: the lookup role disappears into DI plus service discovery, and transport failures surface as HttpRequestException/TaskCanceledException, which the typed client maps to application errors. Keep a hand-written client when the remote mapping needs aggregation or domain translation; a legacy SOAP/WCF contract still uses ChannelFactory<T> or a generated proxy as the delegate.
pitfalls: new HttpClient() per call exhausts sockets (TIME_WAIT); inject the factory-managed client instead.
Capturing a typed client into a singleton while it was registered transient can pin a stale handler - inject the interface, not the raw HttpClient.
Collapsing every HttpRequestException/status into one domain error loses retryable-vs-fatal information; chain the inner exception and keep the status code.

variants.name: Refit source-generated interface client
variants.implementation_notes: Annotate an interface with HTTP attributes and a Roslyn source generator emits the delegate implementation over HttpClient; Refit's DelegatingHandlers carry auth and Polly policies, and ApiException/TransportExceptionFactory translate status and transport failures. Use it when the remote contract is plain HTTP+JSON and the local interface should stay free of hand-written plumbing; hand-write a typed client when the mapping is non-trivial (aggregation, custom error translation).
pitfalls: A generated client is still remote: chatty fine-grained interface methods multiply round trips.
Refit's source generator needs Roslyn 4.8/.NET SDK 8+ at build time; older toolchains fail with REFIT001 or fall back to the reflection package.
Translating ApiException away too early hides retryable 5xx responses; decide the exception factory deliberately.
